items.synopsis: Sending GARP reply packet on a VTEP interface causes flooding in network on QFX5130 and QFX5700 platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved QFX5130 and QFX5700 platforms, Gratuitous Address Resolution Protocol (GARP) flooding occurs in the network when it receives a GARP reply packet on a Virtual Tunnel End Point (VTEP) interface.

items.synopsis: The rpd process crashes when BGP is cleaned up
items.description: On Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, if static default RT-C (Route Target -Constrain) is configured when BGP is cleaned up, the routing process might crash.

items.category: PFE L2 forwarding features on BT based platforms
items.synopsis: Junos OS Evolved PTX platforms fail to relearn MAC after interface mac limit is reached
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved PTX platforms, when 'interface-mac-limit' is configured, the interface fails to learn new MAC addresses when MAC address table gets cleared because the MAC-limit has been reached. This results in disruption of unicast traffic forwarding.

items.category: PFE L2 forwarding features on BT based platforms
items.synopsis: Evolved is using old MAC address for forwarding leading to traffic drops
items.description: On Junos Evolved platforms with VXLAN (Virtual Extensible LAN) configuration, traffic drops because the ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) response is going with old/stale MAC (Media Access Control) address.

items.synopsis: Unstable interface statistic (ingress) going up and down
items.description: The PPS reported for the interface may fluctuate for a few seconds and show either higher or lower value. The chance of this happening is very rare

items.synopsis: Traffic loss is seen on RTG bound interface
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, configuring mac-move with action shutdown can disable the RTG (Redundant Trunk Groups) interface leading to traffic loss bound to that interface.

items.synopsis: Commit error will not be seen after deactivating routing-instance applied under firewall filter
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms with enabled firewall filter, deactivating routing-instance which is already applied under the firewall filter, will not show any commit error after commit is issued. This can be seen occasionally and might impact control plane traffic.

items.synopsis: A high CPU consumption of mcsnoopd process is seen under IGMP-snooping configured scenario leading to its crash
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms with IGMP-snooping (Internet Group Management Protocol) enabled under instance type EVPN (Ethernet Virtual Private Network) with vlan-id=none or unspecified vlan-id there will be a spike in the mcsnoopd process CPU utilization. This will lead to the mcsnoopd process crash and there will be disruptions in the traffic.

items.synopsis: The rpd core is seen in the long-running devices with EVPN enabled
items.description: On Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) community object reference count is not handled properly during the process of remote BGP peer routes update event. The community reference count is increasing during the increment function. However, decrement functions are not called in one of the places after processing the routes update. This will lead to a disturbance of the continuity reference count, which will cause an rpd crash.

items.synopsis: Convergence delay is seen when FPC is offlined under heavy traffic and scaled scenario
items.description: On Junos PTX3000, PTX5000, PTX10008, and PTX10016 routers, when the Flexible PIC Concentrator (FPC) is offlined with scale configuration and heavy traffic, a delay in convergence (into tens of minutes) is seen on all the live FPCs in the chassis other than the offlined one. This impacts traffic.

items.synopsis: Unexpected behavior of bandwidth based metric for IS-IS protocol
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms unexpected behavior of bandwidth based metric in IS-IS is seen since actual bandwidth is falling back to 0 bps when one of the member interface of AE (Aggregated Ethernet) bundle (interface-group) goes down.

items.synopsis: Traffic loop is seen due to incorrect root bridge ID
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, in VSTP (Virtual Spanning-Tree Protocol) topology, whenever a new vlan is added in between previously configured vlan group followed by configuring the system-identifier, the bridge priority will change for existing vlans which might give incorrect system ID or bridge ID creating a traffic loop.

items.synopsis: mac-move-limit : MMAS flag not getting reset after interface recovers due to l2-learning restart
items.description: MMAS Flag will not be displayed for interface after it recovers due to l2-learning process restart

items.synopsis: MVPN tunnel is not synced to backup router
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, when OSPF inter-area is configured with segmented provider-tunnel and master undergoes MBB(make-before-break), the multicast route entry on backup router will not have the tunnel name synced with master.

items.synopsis: Slow convergence of PIM joins causes temporary traffic loss with scaled downstream interfaces
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms with PIM (Protocol Independent Multicast), MVPN (Multicast Virtual Private Network) configured and when the number of downstream interfaces is more than three thousand, slow convergence of PIM joins is seen to take up more of the time and CPU, causing traffic loss for some time.

items.synopsis: Link failure is seen on 10G SFP+ ports of QFX platforms
items.description: On QFX Junos Evolved platforms, the 10G SFP+ ports on specific QFX platforms (QFX5130-32CD, QFX5220-32CD and QFX5220-128C) does not come up even on the normal scenario.

items.category: RPD Next-hop issues including indirect, CNH, and MCNH
items.synopsis: Momentary traffic drop observed for 2 to 3sec while RE switchover
items.description: RE switchover may result in a momentary traffic drop for about 2 to 3 sec, In EVPN-VXLAN setup with EVPN type 5 traffic and NSR configuration.

items.category: RPD route tables, resolver, routing instances, static routes
items.synopsis: Multipath route is not getting compute and skip the multipath eligibility check
items.description: On all Junos platforms, multipath route will not be formed correctly when a BGP route is received from RR (Route Reflector) and preference decided based on cluster list length.

items.synopsis: The rpd process crash will be observed during VPLS to EVPN migration
items.description: On all Junos platforms during VPLS (Virtual Private LAN Service) to EVPN (Ethernet Virtual Private Network) migration, when the EVPN and VPLS are configured under the same routing instance and "instance-type evpn" is enabled, then upon deactivate/delete "protocols vpls" and changing the IFL configuration associated with VPLS will lead to rpd process crash.

items.synopsis: The route leaking does not work between different routing instances by using rib-groups on all Junos OS Evolved platforms
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, if the rib-groups is used to import/export routes into the default routing instance from another routing instance, then connectivity fails between those routing instances.

items.synopsis: The FPC can go to a fault state on certain Junos Evolved PTX platforms after system reboot
items.description: On certain Junos Evolved PTX platforms FPC (Flexible PIC concentrator) goes to a fault state after a system reboots with a Major alarm - Power Failure. This issue is a rare issue and the FPC in a fault state will impact the data traffic. To recover from this issue the impacted FPCs need to be rebooted.

items.synopsis: BNG Controller: L2TP LAC functionality is not working in this release
items.description: L2TP LAC functionality is not working in this release

items.category: UI Infrastructure - mgd, DAX API, DDL/ODL
items.synopsis: The mustd process crash might be observed with persist-group-inheritance
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms configured with persist-group-inheritance, which is enabled by default from 19.4R3 onwards, might lead to mustd process crash in highly scaled configuration.

items.synopsis: < ok/> response is getting generated along with < rpc-error>
items.description: When maximum-password-length is configured and the user tries to configure password whose length exceeds configured maximum-password-length, there is an error and the '' tag is emitted. (Ideally '' tag should not be emitted in an error scenario.) The configuration does not get committed.

items.synopsis: Unable to upgrade Junos using NetConf or Junos script
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, if RPC get-configuration is invoked before RPC request-package-add in the same session of the NETCONF or Junos script, RPC request-package-add will not work.
